newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's SBI index rises for sixth day.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's SBI index rises for sixth day.

text.p: Slovenia's SBI index rose for the sixth day on Thursday, pushed up by an almost six percent jump in bank SKB.

"Most prices are seen as low at the moment, as is the case with SKB, which was also pushed up by today's decision to split its shares. I think SKB could easily rise to up to 50,000 tolars," one trader said.
The SBI index rose 0.77 percent or 9.45 points to 1,237.6.
"I don't think this risnig trend could last over a longer-term as summer time, when trading activity usually calms down, is approaching," said Franci Zmavc, a trader at brokerage Intara.
Overall 10 shares rose, five fell and one was flat, while 13 were untraded. Turnover rose to 71.8 million tolars from 58.8 million.
Traders said turnover remains low, indicating that fresh foreign money is staying away.
Bank SKB was the top gainer and had the highest turnover, jumping 5.98 percent to 45,900 tolars on volume of 494 shares for total turnover of 22.5 million.
The bourse will suspend trading in the share on Friday and Monday due to the bank's stock split.
The bank will split each share, currently with a nominal value of 20,000 tolars ($128), into 20 new shares with a nominal value of 1,000 tolars each.

SKB said the split would be undertaken in order to make it easier for small shareholders to buy its shares and also to bring the nominal value of shares and global depository receipts (GDRs) into line.
In February, SKB became the first Slovenian firm to be traded abroad, listing its GDRs on the London, Frankfurt and Munich stock exchanges, with 20 GDRs representing one share.
Dolenjska bank's preferred share led decliners, falling 3.20 percent to 12,100 tolars on volume of only 86 shares.
Drug producer Lek jumped 3.76 percent to 23,760 tolars on volume of 599 shres for total turnover of 13.9 million tolars. Market participants said Lek's price was still regarded as low.
"Lek was rising steadily over the last week and I think if everything remains like it is it could soon exceed 30,000 tolars," one broker said.
This week alone the share has jumped 6.55 percent. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
